label: Reduction in Practice
notes: Open by framing reduction as a controlled loss of redundant directions. A conserved moment map fixes a level, a group orbit records the direction we collapse, and the reduced Hamiltonian retains exactly the dynamics that survives. Promise the headline example, complex projective space, as a quotient we build by hand today.

label: Marsden-Weinstein Recap
notes: Remind the audience that the quotient of a regular zero level by a free proper action carries a unique symplectic form pulled back from the inclusion. Stress the dimension drop of twice the group rank: we lose one direction to the constraint and one to the orbit for each independent symmetry generator.

label: Why Levels Are Preserved
notes: Walk through the Noether cancellation: invariance kills the Hamiltonian along the group field, the moment map turns that field into a component differential, and the Hamiltonian vector field contracts it into the form. The residual derivative of the moment value along the flow vanishes, so each level is flow-invariant.

label: Reduction at a General Value
notes: Explain that an arbitrary value need not be fixed by the coadjoint action, so point reduction at it can fail. Two cures: orbit reduction quotients the whole coadjoint orbit preimage, and the shifting trick trades a nonzero value for the zero level of an enlarged space crossed with the orbit.

label: The Shifting Trick
notes: Make the shifting trick concrete. Replace reduction of M at the value xi by reduction of the product of M with the coadjoint orbit through xi, carrying the opposite symplectic form, at the zero level. For a torus every level is central, so we may simply subtract a constant from the moment map.

label: CP^n by Reduction
notes: Introduce the marquee example. The circle acts on complex n-plus-one space by simultaneous phase rotation with moment map one half the squared norm. The regular level is the odd sphere, the action is free there, and the quotient is complex projective space. Emphasize that this is reduction done explicitly.

label: The Sphere and the Circle
notes: Detail the geometry: fixing the squared norm pins points to a sphere, and quotienting by the common phase identifies each complex line to a point. The fibers are circles, so projective space is the base of a circle bundle over the sphere. Count dimensions: two n plus one minus one gives two n.

label: Fubini-Study Form
notes: State that the reduced symplectic form on projective space is the Fubini-Study form, the canonical Kahler form descending from the flat form upstairs. Note the normalization tied to the chosen level radius. This is the same form appearing as the symplectic structure on coadjoint orbits of the unitary group.

label: Hopf Picture for n=1
notes: Specialize to n equal one. The five sphere becomes the three sphere, the circle fibers are Hopf circles, and the quotient is the two sphere, the Riemann sphere CP one. Draw the Hopf map so the audience sees reduction as collapsing each linked fiber circle to one base point.

label: Reduction in Mechanics
notes: Connect to dynamics. A cyclic coordinate makes its conjugate momentum conserved; freezing that level and dropping the ignorable angle lowers the phase space dimension by two. Reduction in stages handles a product group one factor at a time, and the staged quotient matches the direct product quotient under freeness.

label: Symplectic Quotient and GIT
notes: Bridge to algebraic geometry. The symplectic quotient M-double-slash-G equals, for the complexified group action, the geometric invariant theory quotient. The Kempf-Ness theorem identifies polystable orbits with zeros of the moment map, so the symplectic and algebraic quotients agree as the same space.

label: Orbifold Warning and Recap
notes: Close with the caveat: a regular level removes infinitesimal stabilizers, but finite stabilizers survive as orbifold singularities, as weighted circle actions show with teardrop and football quotients. Recap the workflow: fix a level, quotient by the orbit, read off the reduced form, and recognize CP^n and GIT quotients as instances.
